faqs.q: Which historical event is credited with initiating the worldwide upsurge of concepts of nationalism and the right of self-determination that influenced Indian nationalism?

Consider the following statements regarding the two-fold effect of political, administrative, and economic unification of India under British rule:
(I) The economic fate of people in different regions became linked together.
(II) Modern transport and communication brought leaders from different regions together for political mobilisation.
Which of the above is/are correct?
The Charter Act, which provided for the addition of six members to the governor-general's council for legislative purposes, was passed in which year?

Consider the following statements regarding Western thought and education as a factor in Indian nationalism:
(I) The English system of education was originally conceived by the rulers in the self-interest of efficient administration.
(II) The English language helped nationalist leaders from different linguistic regions communicate with each other.
Which of the above is/are correct?
According to the chapter, approximately how many newspapers were published in vernacular languages in India in 1877?

Consider the following pairs regarding scholars whose historical researches contributed to the rediscovery of India's past:
(I) Max Mueller – European scholar
(II) R.G. Bhandarkar – Indian scholar
(III) Swami Vivekananda – European scholar
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: Swami Vivekananda is listed among the Indian scholars, not European scholars, who contributed to rediscovering India's past.

faqs.q: Who described the new Indian middle class as "a well-integrated all-India class with varied background but a common foreground of knowledge, ideas and values"?

Consider the following statements regarding the impact of contemporary world movements on Indian nationalism:
(I) The rise of nations on the ruins of the Spanish and Portuguese empires in South America influenced Indian nationalists.
(II) The national liberation movements of Greece and Italy influenced Indian nationalists.
(III) The unification of Germany was a major influence cited.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The chapter cites South America, Greece, Italy, and Ireland specifically; German unification is not mentioned.

faqs.q: Lytton's policy reduced the maximum age limit for the I.C.S. examination from 21 years to how many years, in 1876?

Consider the following statements regarding legislation passed in 1878 that provoked nationalist opposition:
(I) The Vernacular Press Act was passed.
(II) The Arms Act was passed.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Under whose governorship was the Ilbert Bill, seeking to abolish judicial disqualification based on race distinctions, introduced?
What outcome resulted from the stiff opposition of the European community to the Ilbert Bill?

options.b: Ripon had to modify the bill, almost defeating its original purpose
options.d: The bill was passed without any change

faqs.a: Ripon had to modify the bill, almost defeating its original purpose

In 1851, the Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society merged to form:

Consider the following statements regarding the British Indian Association's 1851 petition to the British Parliament:
(I) It demanded establishment of a separate legislature of a popular character.
(II) It demanded abolition of salt duty, abkari, and stamp duties.
(III) It demanded reduction in the age limit for the Indian Civil Service examination.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The demand for reduction of the ICS age limit relates to a later campaign by the Indian Association in 1877, not this 1851 petition.

(I) Surendranath Banerjea
(II) Ananda Mohan Bose
Which of the above is/are correctly identified as founders?

Consider the following pairs regarding founders of the Bombay Presidency Association (1885):
(I) Badruddin Tyabji
(II) Pherozshah Mehta
(III) K.T. Telang
Which of the above is/are correctly identified as its founders?

Consider the following pairs regarding founders of the Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884):
(I) M. Viraraghavachari
(II) B. Subramaniya Aiyer
(III) P. Anandacharlu
Which of the above is/are correctly identified as its founders?
The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, officially established in 1870, grew out of an earlier organisation founded in 1867. What was this earlier organisation called?
faqs.e: The Poona Association (1867) evolved into the formally established Poona Sarvajanik Sabha in 1870, founded by Mahadev Govind Ranade, Ganesh Vasudeo Joshi ('Sarvajanik Kaka'), and S.H. Chiplunkar.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding pre-Congress campaigns:
(I) A campaign was organised for imposition of import duty on cotton in 1875.
(II) A campaign was organised for Indianisation of government service in 1878-79.
(III) A campaign was organised against Lytton's Afghan adventure.
Which of the above is/are correct?
The all-India agitation organised by the Indian Association against the reduction in the maximum age for appearing in the Indian Civil Service examination was popularly known as:
Which Act specifically triggered a pre-Congress campaign for the right to join volunteer corps and against restrictions on plantation labour?
faqs.e: Campaigns against plantation labour conditions were linked specifically to opposition against the Inland Emigration Act.
